releases.title: Ask the Archive Anything
releases.description: You can now bring four decades of shows into Claude and just talk to them. Ask what concerts happened on your birthday, what the archive remembers about a band, every gig at a favorite venue — or let it surprise you with one worth remembering. It answers like the archive itself, in its own voice, always true to the shows that really happened.
highlights: If you use Claude, you can add the archive and ask the way you'd ask a friend — “have you seen Depeche Mode?”, “what happened on June 4th over the years?”, “show me everything at the 9:30 Club”
Get the shape of the whole collection in a sentence — four decades, the bands and rooms it keeps coming back to — or just say “surprise me”
Every answer is grounded in the real shows and told in the archive's own voice — and it's honest when it's just counting from memory
Visit concerts.morperhaus.org/ask.html to see how to connect

releases.title: Liner Notes Tuning & Polish
releases.description: The liner notes feed now surfaces a smarter variety — the same headliner won't reappear too soon, and no single story type will dominate the feed for long. Plus a handful of UI polish fixes accumulated since v4.6.0.
highlights: Liner Notes selection now enforces a 10-post cooldown per headliner — no more seeing the same artist two weeks in a row
Category balance self-corrects: if "I Was There" posts dominate recently, the feed deprioritizes them until the mix evens out
Fixed a data error in The Alarm liner note
How It Works page now scrolls correctly on iPad portrait

releases.title: How It Works
releases.description: Watch three words in a spreadsheet become 42 years of living music history. The new "How It Works" page is an animated cascade that walks you through every API call, enrichment tier, and data transformation — from a raw artist name and venue to artist photos, audio previews, and full setlists — in real time.
highlights: Pick any concert, hit run, and watch the data enrichment cascade pour tier by tier in front of you
Seven tiers reveal how raw inputs become geographic coordinates, artist identity, audio previews, and song-by-song setlists
Slot-machine counters and a post-build glow show the scale of the archive your concert feeds
Auto-loads with a featured Sting concert so you arrive to a live preview, ready to run

releases.title: Mobile Polish
releases.description: The Liner Notes experience on mobile got a proper tune-up. Story cards now show a clean square photo that keeps faces in frame, the share button sits neatly in the footer, and the Liner Notes badge appears inside the artist modal just like it does on desktop.
highlights: Story cards show a square artist photo on all screen sizes — no more cropped heads
Share button moved in-line with deep links, no longer overlapping on small screens
Liner Notes badge appears in the mobile artist modal alongside the On Tour badge

releases.title: Deep Cuts
releases.description: Liner Notes became a full editorial experience — 31 personal essays about your concerts, deep-cut detectors that surface rare finds, and smart notifications that celebrate new posts the moment you return.
highlights: Liner notes in artist gatefold — see every essay for artists you've seen
Year deep links jump straight to any year in your timeline
Mobile bottom nav puts Liner Notes one tap away
Smarter notifications celebrate new liner notes and app updates

releases.title: Liner Notes
releases.description: Forty-two years of concerts, now with stories. Original liner notes drawn from the archive — personal essays, cultural deep cuts, and milestone moments. Browse the feed, filter by category, and subscribe via RSS so new stories come to you.
highlights: New stories every week — anniversary milestones, artist longevity, cultural context, and deep cuts drawn straight from your history
Browse and filter at /liner-notes — category chips, tag filters, and individual post pages at /liner-notes/:slug
App release notes moved to /whats-playing — a cleaner home for what's new in the archive
RSS feed at /liner-notes.xml so new stories come to you automatically

releases.title: Full Coverage
releases.description: iTunes preview coverage reaches 100% across all artists. Search aliases and direct artist ID lookup resolve the remaining edge cases where Apple Music catalog names differ from concert listings.

releases.title: Under the Hood
releases.description: Switched audio previews to iTunes exclusively—stable, permanent URLs with no expiring tokens. Build pipeline now refreshes track data automatically on every run.

releases.title: On Deck
releases.description: Future concerts now get their moment in the spotlight. An upcoming badge appears on Timeline cards and in Artist profiles wherever a show is still ahead—so you always know what's on the horizon.
highlights: Upcoming badge on Timeline cards for concerts still to come
Artist concert history highlights upcoming shows with a distinct badge
Consistent treatment across desktop hover previews and mobile

releases.title: Under the Hood
releases.description: Maintenance update keeping the data pipeline and SEO tools running smoothly behind the scenes.

releases.title: SEO Foundations
releases.description: Search engines now get a clearer picture of your archive—better metadata, structured data, and a baseline for tracking discoverability over time.

releases.title: iOS Home Screen Icons
releases.description: Add the app to your iPhone home screen and it looks the part—custom icons and a proper favicon across every device.
highlights: Custom iOS home screen icon
Favicon optimized for all sizes

releases.title: Documentation Polish
releases.description: Internal documentation updates to keep the project well-documented as it evolves.

releases.title: Mobile Audio Previews
releases.description: Listen to artist previews on your phone—audio playback now works in the mobile Artist view.
highlights: Audio previews in mobile Artist view
Music icon replaces Spotify logo on mobile

releases.title: Artist Scene Polish
releases.description: The Artist Gatefold feels even smoother—refined spacing, larger photos, and more responsive animations make exploring your concert history more immersive. Audio previews now work better on Safari and track your listening patterns to help improve the experience.

releases.title: Audio Preview Player
releases.description: Listen before you go—preview top tracks from 252 artists right in the Artist Gatefold. Get a feel for an artist's sound with 30-second clips from iTunes and Deezer, plus quick links to stream full albums.
highlights: Audio preview player with 30-second clips for 252 artists (99% coverage)
Play/pause controls with animated equalizer and auto-advance
Mobile-responsive design with album art and track details
Direct links to Apple Music and Deezer for full streaming

releases.title: Complete Artist Imagery
releases.description: Every artist who's ever opened a show now has a photo and bio alongside the headliners—no more missing faces in your concert history. We've filled 151 gaps and doubled artist coverage, so you can explore the full story of every show you've attended.
highlights: Opening acts now included—254 artists have photos and bios, up from 104 headliners-only
151 previously missing artists enriched with imagery from expanded sources
Smart name matching finds artists even with complex band names like "Trombone Shorty & Orleans Avenue"
100% artist coverage—every performer in your history now has a face

releases.title: Venue Images Restored
releases.description: Venue photos are back in map popups. Click any venue marker to see its location, concert history, and venue image—the recent SEO update accidentally broke these, but they're working again.

releases.title: By the Numbers
releases.description: Your concert archive now speaks for itself. The Liner Notes page features 12 computed statistics—from most-seen artists to busiest concert year—each linking directly to where you can explore that story. AI agents like ChatGPT and Claude can now quote these facts directly when answering questions about your concert history.
highlights: 12 fact cards display statistics like "Social Distortion: 8 concerts" with deep links
Pre-computed facts in llm.txt help AI agents answer questions about your archive
RSS feed now includes archive statistics with their computed date
Human-friendly detail text like "The most-seen live act, 1990–2024"

releases.title: Comprehensive Testing Infrastructure
releases.description: Added enterprise-grade testing with 305 automated tests covering every data pipeline and interactive scene. When you explore your concert history, you can trust it's been thoroughly validated—from venue geocoding to genre timelines to artist search.
highlights: 268 Vitest tests validate all 26 data processing scripts
37 Puppeteer tests verify every scene interaction and navigation flow
New /test command orchestrates full test suite in under 2 minutes
Testing skill integrated into /implement workflow for new features

releases.title: Discography Data Foundation
releases.description: Built the backend infrastructure to track 15,000+ albums across 247 artists using MusicBrainz. This prepares the groundwork for upcoming discography features—you'll soon be able to explore which albums sparked your concert-going adventures.

releases.title: Quality Standards & Documentation Infrastructure
releases.description: Enhanced Claude Code agent reliability with centralized quality standards and validation guidelines. Behind-the-scenes improvements to ensure consistent, high-quality development workflows.

releases.title: Google Analytics 4 Configuration Fix
releases.description: Fixed Google Analytics event tracking to properly capture user interactions across all scenes. Analytics data now flows correctly to help understand how people explore their concert memories.

releases.title: Map & Venue Navigation Polish
releases.description: Smoother exploration across the venue map and network graph. Fixed several navigation quirks that made it harder to jump between artists and venues, plus cleaned up the map's visual clutter so you can focus on the places that matter most.

releases.title: Connected Experience
releases.description: Navigate seamlessly between scenes by clicking venue names anywhere in the app. When exploring an artist's concert history, tap any venue to jump straight to the Venues scene—automatically spotlighting both the venue and artist to show you their unique relationship. Map markers now display venue names for easier exploration.
highlights: Click venue names in artist details to explore venue-artist relationships
Venue+artist combined deep linking focuses both nodes in force-directed graph
"Explore Venue" buttons now use real links for better mobile UX
Enhanced venue node label visibility in force-directed graph

releases.title: Mobile Artist Experience
releases.description: Artist details now feel native on your phone. Tap any artist card to open a full-screen modal with tabbed navigation—swipe through your concert history, check upcoming tour dates, and pull up setlists with a tap. Swipe down or tap X to close, just like you'd expect.
highlights: Full-screen modal replaces desktop gatefold on phones
Tabbed navigation: Concert History, Upcoming Shows, Top Tracks
Setlist overlay slides in from the right with swipe-to-dismiss
Color-coded tabs with brand accents (violet, amber, Spotify green)

releases.title: iPad Touch Support
releases.description: Explore your concert timeline naturally on iPad with touch-optimized interactions. Drag your finger across concert cards to preview them one by one, then tap to dive into any artist's full history—bringing the same fluid desktop experience to your tablet.
highlights: Drag across timeline cards to preview concerts with haptic feedback
Tap any focused card to jump straight to the artist's gatefold
Smooth touch detection distinguishes taps from swipes automatically

releases.title: Genre Enrichment & Artist Metadata
releases.description: Your genre treemap now includes six more musical styles—from Neo Mellow's chill vibes to Political Hip Hop's conscious messages—giving you a more complete picture of your concert history's sonic diversity.

releases.title: Interactive Timeline Exploration & Genre Journey
releases.description: Click any year on the timeline to explore every concert from that moment, then tap a card to dive into an artist's full story. Plus, watch your musical taste evolve through an animated genre timeline that shows how your concert history shaped your sound.
highlights: Interactive year cards - click any timeline dot to see all concerts from that year
One-tap navigation from timeline to artist gatefold details
Animated genre treemap with decade-by-decade musical evolution
Genre drill-down to explore artists within each musical style

releases.title: Real-Time Tour Dates with Ticketmaster
releases.description: Discover when your favorite artists are touring and buy tickets instantly with live Ticketmaster integration
highlights: Live tour dates via Ticketmaster Discovery API (5,000 calls/day)
"ON TOUR" badge appears instantly when artist has upcoming shows
Direct ticket purchase links for every concert
24-hour smart caching with automatic artist name fallback

releases.title: Developer Experience & Documentation Overhaul

highlights: Two-path getting started guide (Quick Start vs Your Own Data)
Example CSV templates for concert data and venue status
Unified data format specifications in data/README.md
Privacy-first: Personal data files now gitignored with examples in repo

Auto-scroll to artist and open gatefold
Default sort by times seen (most frequent first)
